correctness.rationale: Any nonfixed three-periodic trajectory on a connected graph is fully cycling; otherwise a permanently resting vertex adjacent to a cycling vertex would be excited. Full cycling is equivalent to each vertex having a next-phase neighbor. On S(H), each unlike-colored original edge has exactly one optional helping assignment, helpful to one endpoint only, making the nonempty-choice factors disjoint. A finite functional digraph gives a simple cycle of length divisible by three, and spanning-forest extension gives the converse. The multinomial K_n formula follows by class sizes. Two separately constructed verifiers matched 774927 complete-state tests and all 43 connected labelled graphs through four original vertices. Bounds, edge cases and quantifiers were checked.

value.rationale: The result resolves a natural initially recurrent-state invariant on every connected full subdivision S(H). The exact existence threshold is the intrinsic cycle-length-divisibility condition in H, and the factorization determines all primitive three-periodic states even when the subdivided graph has many overlapping cycles. It yields a complete labelled count for every subdivided complete graph and explains the sharp absence for S(K_{2,b}) versus existence for S(K_{3,b}) when b≥3. These are motivated by recurrent excitation waves; no significance is asserted for other periods or long-time basins.
